matching_id_or_code.title: Stability of Peaked Reduced Ostrovsky Waves
matching_id_or_code.statement: For the reduced Ostrovsky equation, are the peaked periodic traveling waves $$U_*(z)=\frac{3z^2-\pi^2}{18},$$ extended periodically, nonlinearly stable or unstable?
matching_id_or_code.background:
Collected from Oberwolfach Reports, which document mathematical workshops and their open-problem discussions.

**Source report:** [Mathematical Theory of Water Waves (2020), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2019/32, pp. 1919--1979](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2019/32)

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-22)

**Status:** partially solved

**Assessment.** Linear and spectral instability, together with uniqueness, are proved for the peaked periodic wave, but nonlinear instability and the full nonlinear stability question remain open.

**Sources checked.**

- [Geyer--Pelinovsky, linear instability](https://doi.org/10.1137/18M117978X)
- [Geyer--Pelinovsky, spectral instability](https://doi.org/10.1090/proc/14937)
- [original OWR report](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2019/32)

This is a dated literature triage derived from the supplied OWR curation; verify time-sensitive status and cited claims independently.
